chunks: And from a letter of him (peace be upon him) to Talha and az-Zubayr (through 'Imran ibn al-Husayn al-Khuzai).

key_terms.الزُّبَيْر: Az-Zubayr, a prominent companion of the Prophet.
key_terms.الْخُزَاعِيُّ: Al-Khuzai, referring to the tribe of the messenger.
key_terms.طَلْحَة: Talha, a prominent companion of the Prophet.
key_terms.عِمْرَانُ بْنُ الْحُصَيْنِ: Imran ibn al-Husayn, the messenger mentioned.

ai.seo_question: Who was the messenger for Imam Ali's letter to Talha and Zubayr?
ai.summary: This heading introduces the seminal letter from Imam Ali (AS) to Talha and al-Zubayr, delivered by 'Imran ibn al-Husayn, marking a pivotal moment in the early Caliphate as Ali sought to consolidate authority and clarify governance principles. It sets the stage for a comprehensive discourse on political ethics, distinguishing between the rights of the ruler and the obligations of the ruled, which remains a cornerstone of Shia political jurisprudence.
